Exam mechanics are HEDGED: the fetched official Tennessee manual never discloses a specific number of items per knowledge test (general knowledge or any endorsement) or an explicit passing-score percentage anywhere in its text -- confirmed by exhaustive keyword search of the full extracted manual for 'questions', 'percent', '80%', 'passing score', and similar terms, which surfaced zero matches (only generic references like 'these questions may be on the test' after each section's self-review list, with no item count or score threshold ever stated). The official TN CDL Division webpage (tn.gov/safety/driver-services/commercial-driver-license.html) similarly states only that knowledge tests 'may include a combination vehicles test, air brakes test, and applicable exams for endorsements in addition to the general knowledge test' without stating counts. The federally standardized 80% minimum passing score under 49 CFR 383.135(a) applies regardless. Third-party CDL test-prep aggregators (not used as a source for any question content, only cited here as corroboration since Tennessee's own sources are silent) converge on a conventional 50-question/40-correct(80%) General Knowledge format consistent with the shared AAMVA base manual used by other CDL-track states in this project, but this specific item count is NOT asserted as an officially confirmed Tennessee figure anywhere in this question bank's source citations, per this project's no-default-values discipline. What IS confirmed directly from Tennessee's own manual: Tennessee CLPs are valid for 365 days and cannot be converted after expiration (all knowledge and skills tests become null and void); a CLP must be held at least 14 days before the skills test; a failed knowledge test may be retaken the next day (cheating applicants are held to a DSC-manager-determined wait instead); a no-show for a scheduled DSC test requires a 45-day wait to reschedule; CDL/CLP applicants must be at least 21, with an exception effective July 1, 2022 allowing 18-20-year-olds to operate a Class A or B CMV intrastate without any endorsement; ELDT (Entry-Level Driver Training, effective February 7, 2022) is required for a first-time Class A/B CDL, a B-to-A upgrade, or a first-time passenger/school-bus/hazmat endorsement, with exemptions for pre-2/7/2022 CDL/S/P/H holders and for CLP holders who convert before their permit expires; the CDL Skills Test has three segments (vehicle inspection, basic vehicle control, on-road driving) taken in order, each must be passed before advancing, and typically takes about two hours; Tennessee's CDL Skills Test 'What to Study' table (Figure 1.2) maps each class/endorsement to specific manual sections, confirming the same 13-section structure used across this project's other CDL-track states. Tennessee uses the standard federal three-class system (Class A/B/C) and the standard six CDL endorsements -- the manual's own Section 1 text states 'There are six kinds of CDL endorsements': H (Hazardous Materials, requires a TSA fingerprint-based background check), N (Tank Vehicle, >119-gallon individual/1,000-gallon aggregate capacity threshold), P (Passenger, 16+ passenger design capacity), T (Doubles/Triples), X (combined Tank + Hazmat), and S (School Bus, any class A/B/C); only P, S, and N may be added to a CLP (P/S endorsements require a companion 'no passengers' P-restriction on the CLP; N requires a companion 'no cargo' X-restriction on the CLP). Tennessee confirms 'ten standardized restriction codes' (E no manual transmission, K intrastate only, L no air-brake CMV, M no Class A passenger vehicle, N no Class A/B passenger vehicle, O no fifth-wheel tractor-trailer, P no passengers in CMV bus, V medical variance, X no cargo in tank vehicle, Z no full-air-brake CMV) -- all ten definitions drafted directly from the manual's own restriction-code table. Disqualification detail confirmed from Section 1.3: 1-year CDL loss (3 years if hazmat-placarded, life for a second offense or a controlled-substance felony) for BAC .04%+/DUI/refusal/leaving-the-scene/CMV-felony/fatality-by-negligence; a 24-hour out-of-service order for any detectable BAC under .04%; 60/120-day CDL loss for two/three-or-more serious traffic violations in 3 years; out-of-service-order violations carry a source-text tracked-changes/bracket artifact identical in kind to ones this project has resolved in other states' manuals (Louisiana's '90 180 days,' Oregon's bracketed 90-day figure) -- Tennessee's own text literally reads '[For at least 90 days if you have committed your first violation... in a ten-year period]' as one unbroken bracketed block (1 year for a second violation in 10 years, 3 years for a third or more); 60/120-day/1-year CDL loss for first/second/third railroad-highway grade-crossing violations within 3 years; hazmat endorsement is denied/lost for non-permanent-residency, US citizenship renunciation, certain felony indictments/convictions, mental-capacity adjudication, or a TSA security-threat determination; a personal-vehicle license revocation for alcohol/controlled-substance/felony violations costs 1 year of CDL privileges (life for a second such violation in either vehicle type); other confirmed rules include the one-CDL-only rule ($5,000 fine/jail for violation), 30-day employer/agency conviction-notification windows, 2-business-day suspension-notification window, a 10-year employment-history requirement for CDL job applications, hand-held-phone and texting bans while driving, mandatory seatbelt use, and IRP/IFTA registration obligations for interstate CMVs. Content-depth rationale: Tennessee uses the same AAMVA-authored 'CDL Driver's Manual, 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017' base document used by several other CDL-track states already built in this project (e.g. Louisiana, New Mexico), organized into the same 13 core sections -- Section 1 Introduction, Section 2 Driving Safely (the largest section by far, split here into two buckets: 02_driving_safely_a covering subsections 2.1 Vehicle Inspection through 2.16 Mountain Driving, 03_driving_safely_b covering 2.17 Driving Emergencies through the Hazardous Materials Rules for All Drivers subsection that closes the section), Section 3 Transporting Cargo Safely, Section 4 Transporting Passengers Safely, Section 5 Air Brakes, Section 6 Combination Vehicles, Section 7 Doubles and Triples, Section 8 Tank Vehicles (a genuinely short, dense 2-page section in this manual), Section 9 Hazardous Materials (the second-largest section, split into two buckets: 10_hazmat_a covering 9.1 Intent of the Regulations through 9.4 Loading and Unloading, 11_hazmat_b covering 9.5 Bulk Packaging Marking through 9.7 Hazardous Materials Emergencies, explicitly excluding the 9.8 Glossary since the manual states in its own text 'Note: You will not be tested on this glossary'), Section 10 School Buses, Section 11 Vehicle Inspection Test, and Section 12 Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test combined with Section 13 On-Road Driving into one bucket (this manual documents the skills-test scoring system -- encroachments, pull-ups, outside-vehicle 'looks' capped at two except one for Straight Line Backing, and final-position requirements -- and all six control exercises: Straight Line Backing, Offset Back/Right, Offset Back/Left, Parallel Park Driver Side, Parallel Park Conventional, and Alley Dock -- in unusually explicit detail). Sections naturally short in this manual (Cargo: 22 questions, Tank Vehicles: 18, Doubles/Triples: 27, Passenger: 30) were sized down accordingly rather than padded to match larger sections; Driving Safely (135 questions across two buckets), Hazardous Materials (101 across two buckets), Air Brakes (65), School Bus (68), Combination Vehicles (55), and Vehicle Inspection (52) supported deeper coverage and were sized up accordingly, reflecting genuine manual depth rather than an artificial per-bucket target. Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official Tennessee manual text cited in that question's source_note; none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's numbers -- the top-level agent independently re-verified every one of the 14 bucket files against the source text and JSON schema (structural field checks, 4-distinct-choices checks, and a per-file answer-letter tally), confirming 677 total drafted questions, zero structural errors, zero exact-duplicate questions across the bank, and every file's correct_choice distribution within the required 15-35% per-letter band before the batch build was run.
